newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down in dull trading.

text.p: Shanghai B shares closed down in sluggish trade on Friday, with most investors on the sidelines waiting for market-moving news, brokers said.
The index fell 0.303 point or 0.60 percent to 50.152 points, on volume of 7.3 million shares worth $2.8 million. Of 41 B shares, 32 traded, with 12 down, 12 flat and eight up.
Brokers said that there was speculation among domestic investors that the government would announce restrictions on local investors trading foreign currency B shares.
Officials have declined comment on the rumours which have been circulating for months.
Shanghai Worldbest traded the most, ending unchanged at $0.296, on volume of 929,800 shares.
Shanghai A shares closed up sharply on a technical rebound but trading was slow on cautious sentiment, brokers said.
The A index rose 23.786 points or 3.01 percent to 814.600 points, on volume of 264.7 million shares worth 2.2 billion yuan. The SSE 30 rose 59.023 points or 2.92 percent to 2078.044 points.
Shanghai Donghai was the star, surging 1.19 yuan or 11.90 percent to 11.19 yuan, on volume of 3.5 million shares.
"The market became very sluggish without trading by domestic investors," one broker said. "Overseas selling pushed the index down."
"The market has continued falling for nine days and will rebound technically in the short term if there is no negative news," a second broker said.

Eastern Communications was the worst performer after it announced that, to support the share price, it had bought back 15 million shares from the market to distribute to shareholders as part of a private placement, brokers said. It fell $0.040 or 5.26 percent to $0.720, on volume of 376,000 shares.
